judge: pointjudge: two readers, two passes each, one decider
uncovered_described: No taxonomy code covers an agent treating the absence of counter-evidence in supplied passages as positive confirmation of a claim (argument from ignorance) when no explicit input fact is misread and no external fact is introduced; SP_02 explicitly excludes 'an invalid logical inference from provided text ... without introducing outside facts.'
No taxonomy code covers this argument-from-ignorance style inference (absence of evidence read as confirmation) when no explicit passage fact is misread and no outside fact is introduced.

The taxonomy has no code for a premature/unsupported truth verdict reached without any passage evidence of the compared quantity, distinct from misreading provided text (SP_02 explicitly excludes inconsistent-verdict cases where passages were read correctly).
The taxonomy has no code for concluding a claim is true merely from absence of contrary evidence rather than from affirmative supporting evidence.

No taxonomy code covers using the assertion embedded in the claim under test as evidence for itself; this is not a distortion of supplied passages (SP_02, since the passages say nothing about this director to distort) nor an introduction of outside facts (SP_01, since no new entity or fact is introduced).

No taxonomy code covers rendering an affirmative verdict on a claim whose key component (the unnamed director's identity/nationality) has no supporting evidence at all in the passages; this is an unsupported conclusion, not a misreading of what the passages say (SP_02) nor an injected external fact (SP_01).
A mode for treating absence-of-evidence as affirmative evidence for a claim (an inference fallacy distinct from misreading explicit text or importing outside facts) is not covered by the taxonomy.
Same uncovered mechanism as the turn-1 instance: absence-of-evidence treated as confirming evidence, not a misreading of explicit text nor an import of outside facts.

No code covers an internally self-contradictory assertion that manufactures a nonexistent 'error' about a correctly-read fact, without introducing external content, distorting the source passages, or affecting the final verdict/query.

No taxonomy code covers treating absence of contradicting evidence in the passages as affirmative confirmation of a claim (an absence-of-evidence-as-evidence-of-truth fallacy); the agent neither misreads explicit text nor imports outside facts, so SP_02/SP_01 do not apply.
No taxonomy code covers concluding a claim is true from mere silence in the retrieved passages rather than from explicit contradicting or confirming evidence.

A mode for drawing an affirmative verdict from the mere absence of contradicting evidence (treating silence as proof of a negative) rather than from an actual misreading of supplied text or introduction of outside facts; SP_02's own do-not-use clause explicitly excludes invalid logical inference of this kind.

No taxonomy code covers an invalid inference rule (treating non-contradiction in unrelated passages as positive confirmation of an unverified claim) that neither misreads specific passage content nor introduces a new external fact.

No taxonomy code covers a pure key-ordering deviation inside an otherwise well-formed, fully parseable JSON object; this is a violation of an explicit instructed order with no functional/parsing consequence, distinct from delimiter corruption (SP_10) or container mismatch (SP_04).

No code covers drawing a positive conclusion from the mere absence of contradicting evidence in the supplied passages; SP_02 explicitly excludes invalid logical inferences from provided text that introduce no outside facts, and SP_01 requires an introduced external fact, which is not present here.

No code covers an invalid inference from the absence of information in the supplied passages; SP_02 explicitly excludes this (invalid inference without introducing outside facts), and SP_13 requires treating a prior-turn assertion as fact, but here the agent independently re-derives the same fallacious conclusion from the newly retrieved passages themselves, not merely by propagating the prior summary.

No taxonomy code covers an unsupported, premature verdict rendered from a correctly-read passage set: the agent does not misread the supplied text (SP_02 excludes 'rendering an inconsistent overall verdict despite correctly reading the passages'), introduce outside facts (SP_01), or halt execution (SP_12, which concerns the agent itself stopping the task, not a downstream summary overclaiming); the gap is a verdict asserted beyond what the evidence in hand supports.

An invalid-inference mechanism: the agent draws an unsupported affirmative conclusion from the mere absence of a stated fact in correctly-read passages, without misreading any explicit statement and without importing outside facts, which SP_02 explicitly excludes and no other code covers.

Same invalid-inference mechanism as in turn 1: an unsupported affirmative conclusion drawn from absence of a stated fact, not a misreading of explicit text and not an imported external fact, which existing codes explicitly exclude.

No taxonomy code covers an argument-from-silence inference (absence of a stated fact treated as confirming a claim); SP_02 explicitly excludes invalid logical inferences drawn from provided text when no outside fact is introduced.
Same gap as the turn-1 point: no code exists for concluding a claim is true from the mere absence of contradicting evidence rather than from a positive fact.

This is a task-comprehension failure that causes the agent to substitute an irrelevant output for the one required: it is not a misreading of a specific fact or relationship in the passages (SP_02), not a functional field-type mismatch since the summary field still holds a summary-shaped text (SP_03), and not a premature halt since the turn completed fully (SP_12). No code in the taxonomy addresses an agent hallucinating ambiguity in a well-formed input and consequently performing a different task than the one it was given.
No taxonomy code covers a reasoning-field comprehension failure where the agent misidentifies the step's objective itself (as opposed to malforming or mistyping an output field).

The taxonomy explicitly excludes exactly this mechanism (invalid logical inference from provided text without introducing outside facts) from SP_02, and no other code covers an absence-of-evidence-treated-as-evidence-of-absence fallacy that manufactures a definitive verdict the passages do not support.

No taxonomy code covers an agent mistaking two sequential multi-hop summaries, which are cumulative evidence, for two competing/alternative outputs needing comparison; this is a misunderstanding of the functional role of its own declared inputs, not a misread of facts contained within them, not introduced external knowledge, and not itself a query-construction or formatting defect.

No code covers a verdict that treats a multi-part claim as fully supported while silently failing to check one of its explicit sub-claims (nationality) against passages that were otherwise read correctly; SP_02 explicitly excludes 'an inconsistent overall verdict despite correctly reading the passages.'

No code covers a final verdict statement that is self-contradictory with a fact explicitly stated in the same output, when the source passages were otherwise read correctly; this is the exact case SP_02's exclusion clause carves out.

The taxonomy has no code for reaching an unwarranted 'supported' verdict through an invalid inference built entirely from correctly-read, provided passages (no external facts are introduced, and it is not a simple misreading of an explicit stated fact — it is faulty reasoning about what the passages establish).
As in turn 1, the taxonomy has no code for an unwarranted 'supported' verdict reached via faulty inference from correctly-read passages without introducing external facts.

No taxonomy code covers a false-negative verdict drawn from mere absence of evidence in an incomplete, single-hop retrieval; SP_02 explicitly excludes invalid logical inference, and no external fact was introduced to ground this particular conclusion.

This is an invalid logical inference drawn from correctly-read passages: the agent accurately notes no comparison data exists for the Margulis-lemma founder, then still renders an unsupported comparative verdict. SP_02's own exclusion clause rules it out ('do not use when the agent draws an invalid logical inference from provided text ... without introducing outside facts' / 'renders an inconsistent overall verdict despite correctly reading the passages'), and no other code in the taxonomy covers an unsupported conclusion reached without misreading explicit text or importing external facts.

No taxonomy code covers rendering a confident 'supported'/'refuted' verdict when the agent's own reasoning admits the decisive evidence is missing from the passages; this is an overconfidence/soundness failure distinct from merely introducing an external fact.

No code covers declaring a claim fully 'supported'/'confirmed' while a specific claim element is simply never addressed by the passages (no misreading occurred, and SP_02 explicitly excludes an inconsistent verdict reached from correctly-read passages; no external fact was invented, so SP_01 does not apply either).

No code covers an invalid inference that treats the absence of contradicting evidence in retrieved passages as positive confirmation of an unverified claim premise, when no new external fact is introduced (SP_01 explicitly excludes pure invalid-inference cases, and SP_02 requires a misreading of explicit supplied content, which did not occur here).
No code covers an invalid inference that treats absence of evidence in newly retrieved passages as positive confirmation of a claim, without introducing any new external fact.

No taxonomy code covers inferring a claim's truth from the mere absence of contradicting information in the passages; SP_01 is explicitly for introduced external facts (none are introduced here) and SP_02 is for misreading text actually present, not for filling an evidentiary gap with an unwarranted inference.

No taxonomy code covers a stray/garbled extraneous token inserted into otherwise coherent generated prose; this is a low-level generation corruption, not a misreading of input, an external-knowledge injection, or a schema/delimiter problem.

No taxonomy code covers word-level text corruption/garbling produced during generation; it is not a misreading of the passages (the underlying claim 'male' is correct), not external knowledge, and not a structural/schema fault.

No code covers overclaiming full confirmation of a multi-part sub-claim when one component (here, the 'broad-leafed' descriptor) is never addressed by the cited passage, absent any misreading of explicit text or introduction of outside facts.

No code covers an unsupported affirmative verdict reached by treating the absence of a specified count as proof the count differs, when the passages themselves were read correctly and no external fact was introduced.
Same gap as the turn 1 instance: no code addresses overclaiming confirmation of an unaddressed descriptor within a compound claim.
Same gap as the turn 1 instance: no code covers an affirmative verdict built on the absence of a stated count.

The taxonomy's closest codes (SP_01, SP_02) explicitly exclude 'invalid logical inference from provided text without introducing outside facts' and 'inconsistent verdict despite correctly reading the passages' — which is exactly what happened here (passages [1] and [3] were read correctly, but the leap to a settled genus-level verdict for an unconfirmed entity is uncovered by any code).

No taxonomy code covers an agent's reasoning field misidentifying the fundamental nature of its own task (treating a retrieval-query-generation step as a summary-comparison/evaluation step) independently of the query text that results from it.

The taxonomy has no code for an invalid inference drawn purely from the absence of information (argument from ignorance): SP_01 requires introducing outside facts, which did not happen, and SP_02 explicitly excludes invalid logical inferences drawn from provided text when no outside facts are introduced.
No taxonomy code covers an invalid inference from the mere absence of a stated fact in the passages; SP_02 explicitly excludes this when no external fact is introduced.
No taxonomy code captures adopting an unwarranted reasoning shortcut that exempts one conjunct of a compound claim from evidentiary verification merely because the claim itself asserts it.
No taxonomy code captures declaring full support for a compound claim while one of its conjunct entities has zero supporting evidence in the passages.

No taxonomy code covers an agent's reasoning field asserting an action is impossible while its own output field performs that exact action; this is a reasoning/output self-contradiction, distinct from query-content or schema-formatting failures.

No taxonomy code covers a verdict-level conclusion that is inconsistent with (i.e., unsupported by) the evidence despite the agent having correctly read the passages it did use; SP_02 explicitly excludes this kind of inconsistent-verdict case.

appended.note: SP_15 assignments lifted from pointjudge-2 (tax-15, one reader, no decider) onto the pointjudge-1 mapping. The two runs used different judge shapes, so SP_15's counts here were produced by a different process than the other 14 codes' and are not on the same footing.
